\item \textbf{Microscaling-format instabilities} (Su, Kwun, Gil, Kakade \& Anand, 2025, \citep{arxiv:2506.20752}, "Characterization and Mitigation of Training Instabilities in Microscaling Formats") characterizes format-induced instability modes under low precision. The shared \emph{premise} --- that the format channel is a meaningful intervention in its own right and deserves controlled ablation --- is consistent with F2's analytical framing. We do not claim the methodologies coincide (Su et al. is not a Pearl-CDE paper); we cite it as evidence that the format channel itself is an active area for ablation work, which motivates the format-zoo arm in \cref{sec:9.4}.
\item \textbf{MXFP4 on native FP4 hardware} (Cim, Palangappa, Hodak, Dwivedula, Arunachalam \& Kandemir, 2026, \citep{arxiv:2605.09825}, "Pretraining Large Language Models with MXFP4 on Native FP4 Hardware") is the first non-emulated MXFP4 pretraining and reports convergence-token overhead on AMD MI355X silicon. We cite it as the MXFP4 hardware anchor: the BPB-vs-compute frontier for FP4 is now measurable on real hardware rather than only on emulated grids.
\item \textbf{Fibonacci-code-word quantization} (Fiandaca \& Gomony, 2025, \citep{arxiv:2511.01921}, "Fibbinary-Based Compression and Quantization for Efficient Neural Radio Receivers") is the only published Fibonacci-binary quantization work we are aware of in any domain. It applies to neural radio receivers, not transformer LLMs; we cite it as a methodological anchor --- Fibonacci-style encodings have at least one published precedent outside transformers --- but not as evidence that phi-style training is established practice for language models.
\item \textbf{Posit number system} (Gustafson \& Yonemoto, 2017, \emph{Supercomputing Frontiers and Innovations} 4(2):71--86, "Beating Floating Point at its Own Game: Posit Arithmetic") is the standards reference for the Posit16 (es=1, useed=4) arm of the format-zoo benchmark. Our companion crate ships a standards-compliant Posit16 codec. We report only an \textbf{encode-time} reconstruction-fidelity microbenchmark as a preregistration anchor; the headline grid table appears below this bullet list.
\end{itemize}

\#\#\#\# 9.4.1 Posit16 vs GF16 encode-time grid (preregistration anchor)

To fix the format-zoo configuration \emph{before} any training data is
collected for the champion-scale follow-up, we report an
\textbf{encode-time only} reconstruction-fidelity microbenchmark. The
binary \texttt{src/bin/format\_microbench} round-trips a synthetic
embedding matrix of shape \texttt{(vocab=128, d\_model)} through each
format and reports the relative L2 error
\texttt{sqrt(sum\_sq\_err / sum\_sq\_signal)} along with the count of values
that underflowed to zero. The grid spans
\texttt{d\_model in \{128, 384, 768, 1024\}} $\times$ init scheme $\in$ `{xavier, he,
normal\_002}` $\times$ 5 seeds = 60 cells; full per-cell JSON is in
\texttt{.trinity/results/format\_microbench\_grid/}, gated for freshness
by a dedicated CI stage (the 41st in \texttt{run\_all\_checks.sh}).

The headline measurement is $\Delta$ relative L2 of Posit16 vs GF16,
mean $\pm$ sample-std across the 5 seeds. The Monte Carlo standard
error is \texttt{std/√5 \~\{\} 0.45 x std} (so the MC error is roughly half
of the $\pm$ figure shown, not half of the delta itself). All deltas
reported below sit between $-$70.6\% and $-$88.6\%, while the largest
sample-std is 0.26\%; the implied MC error is at most ~0.12\%, so
every delta is more than 500$\times$ its MC error and significance is
overdetermined at this N.

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\begin{tabular}{lllll}
\toprule
init scheme & d=128 & d=384 & d=768 & d=1024 \\
\midrule
\texttt{xavier} & $-$83.2 $\pm$ 0.08\% & $-$74.1 $\pm$ 0.14\% & $-$72.8 $\pm$ 0.12\% & $-$70.6 $\pm$ 0.07\% \\
\texttt{he} & $-$88.6 $\pm$ 0.06\% & $-$85.4 $\pm$ 0.06\% & $-$82.9 $\pm$ 0.09\% & $-$81.5 $\pm$ 0.02\% \\
\texttt{normal\_002} & $-$72.2 $\pm$ 0.26\% & $-$72.1 $\pm$ 0.17\% & $-$72.1 $\pm$ 0.08\% & $-$72.2 $\pm$ 0.01\% \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}


\textbf{What the table says}: at the small-magnitude regime typical of
embedding initialization, the \textbf{encode-time} round-trip from f32
to Posit16 back to f32 has \emph{lower} relative L2 error than the same
round-trip through GF16, for every combination of d\_model and init
scheme in the grid. The reported delta is a property of the codec
applied to the init distribution, not a training-time outcome; we
return to the encode-vs-train distinction at the end of the
sub-subsection. The \texttt{he} row shows the largest win
(d\_model-scaled $\sigma$ = √(2/d\_model) puts the average magnitude near
the boundary of GF16's underflow region); \texttt{normal\_002} is
regime-independent of d\_model (fixed $\sigma$ = 0.02 doesn't scale with
d\_model, so format-quality at fixed magnitude stays put). GF16
underflows $\approx$ 55--70 of 49 152 values to zero per Xavier-init seed
at d\_model = 384; Posit16 underflows zero values in any cell of
the grid because the standards-compliant saturation rule rounds
small magnitudes to MIN\_POS = \texttt{4\^\{\}-14} rather than to zero.

\textbf{What the table does NOT say}: nothing here is a training-time
result. The encode-time microbench measures the \emph{codec}, not the
\emph{recipe}; whether a +74\% reduction in relative L2 at the
embedding-init regime translates into a measurable BPB delta after
a champion-scale training run is the question the preregistered
follow-up in \texttt{docs/F2\_PRE\_REG.md} is designed to test. We report
the grid \emph{only} to lock in the format-zoo configuration (\texttt{Posit16}
vs \texttt{GF16} at d\_model = 384, Xavier init, 5 seeds) before training
artifacts are produced, in the same spirit as W3C-PROV preambles
on the empirical CSVs (\cref{sec:3.5.1}).

\textbf{Methodological footnotes} for the table above:
(i) Sample-std heterogeneity across cells (0.01--0.26\%) reflects
init-dependent magnitude spread --- the \texttt{he} row at large d\_model
sits in the cleanest regime ($\sigma$ scales as 1/√d\_model), while
\texttt{normal\_002} at all d\_model and \texttt{xavier} at d=128 sit at
boundaries where small per-seed magnitude variations matter
relatively more.
(ii) The 5-seed budget was chosen to keep MC error at least 1.5
orders of magnitude below the smallest delta; if a future
revision requires tighter bounds (e.g., to detect a hypothetical
+1\% delta), the budget must grow as the inverse square of the
target delta.
(iii) RNG choice --- we use a deterministic LCG (Numerical Recipes
parameters) seeded per cell. A real-RNG version would differ in
the tail of the distribution; the distinction is immaterial here
because format-quality at the magnitudes typical of init
distributions depends on the bulk, not the tail. Reproducibility
is the load-bearing property, and LCG seeding provides it
bit-exactly across machines.



\section{Conclusion + venue calibration}\label{sec:10}



\subsection{Conclusion}\label{sec:10.1}


We have argued --- and empirically demonstrated on a sandbox-scale
ablation matrix --- that the standard seed-mean ablation practice in ML
systematically misattributes effects when one intervention mediates
another. The Loop 49 RmsNorm sign flip (canonical NDE $-$4.12 BPB $\to$ wd0
CDE +0.43 BPB) is a single concrete instance; the framework that
produced it (Pearl-style stratified CDE + the Daniel et al. (2015)
four-path decomposition + delta-method SE + bridge-score sensitivity
envelope + cross-stratum stability flag) is generic and ready for
re-use on any
ablation question where a suppression-mediator may be present.

The cost is modest: ~25 minutes of compute per stratum at sandbox scale,
ten binaries sharing a stable CSV contract, and 830 tests including
formula-locking regression tests for the identification arithmetic.
The payoff --- a sign correction on a well-known fix --- is qualitatively
larger than the cost.

We do not claim that RmsNorm "is" or "is not" useful at champion scale;
the sandbox result reframes the question, it does not answer it. The
champion-scale follow-up is pre-registered in \texttt{docs/F2\_PRE\_REG.md}.
What we do claim is that \textbf{any ablation paper proposing a methodology change without checking for suppression is publishing a number that could be off by a factor of 10 in magnitude or wrong in sign}. The
framework is open-source under MIT; reviewers and follow-up authors
should consider it a default first step before reporting seed means.


\subsection{Venue calibration}\label{sec:10.2}


We map four candidate venues against the contribution profile:

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{NeurIPS MLRC (reproducibility track) --- primary target.} Required artifacts: W3C-PROV preambles (\cref{sec:3.5.1}), formula-locking regression tests (\cref{sec:8.2}), reviewer reproducibility checklist (\cref{sec:3.5.4}). The paper's load-bearing contribution is the reproducibility-grade discipline around stratified Pearl-CDE analysis, which directly matches this track's mission.
\item \textbf{NeurIPS Causal-ML Workshop --- fallback.} A re-balanced version would lead with \cref{sec:3.2} (Daniel et al. four-PSE) and \cref{sec:3.3} (bridge-score) and de-emphasize \cref{sec:3.5} (provenance), shifting focus from infrastructure to identification theory.
\item \textbf{ICML main track --- future.} Requires either a successful Phase 1 champion-scale sweep per \texttt{docs/F2\_PRE\_REG.md}, or F2 re-applied to a second publicly-debated ablation finding. Either path is outside the present submission scope.
\item \textbf{Stat journals (Biometrics, Stat. Med., JCI) --- aspirational.} Requires a stat-grade simulation study or domain co-author; the methodological bar is set by recent work such as Guo et al. (2026, \emph{Statistics in Medicine}, doi:10.1002/sim.70548).
\end{itemize}

Submission logistics (deadlines, OpenReview / Google Form URLs,
registration paths) are tracked separately in
\texttt{papers/SUBMISSION\_CHECKLIST.md} and intentionally kept out of
the manuscript body.

\section{Reproducible commands}\label{app:a}

\section{Provenance preamble format}\label{app:b}


Every CSV emitted by an F2 binary opens with a W3C-PROV / RO-Crate
preamble of the form documented in \cref{sec:3.5.1}. The full record is six
lines of \texttt{\# prov:*} keys plus optional auxiliary fields. The validator
in \texttt{src/bin/f2\_provenance\_check.rs} enforces the contract.

\textbf{B.1 Required keys:}

\begin{table}[h]
\centering
\begin{tabular}{lll}
\toprule
Key & Value & Validation \\
\midrule
\texttt{\# prov:generatedAt} & Unix seconds UTC, integer & Must parse as \texttt{u64}. \\
\texttt{\# prov:wasGeneratedBy} & Full command line of the producing binary & Free text; surfaced in the audit trail. \\
\texttt{\# prov:agent\_git\_sha} & 7-char or 40-char git SHA at producer time & \texttt{WARN} if SHA differs from current \texttt{HEAD}; \texttt{PASS} otherwise. \\
\texttt{\# prov:trainer\_internals\_schema} & Versioned schema string, e.g. \texttt{trainer\_internals\_v1\_2026\_06\_01} & Must match the producer's \texttt{TRAINER\_INTERNALS\_SCHEMA}. \texttt{FAIL} (exit 2) on mismatch. \\
\texttt{\# prov:cargo\_pkg\_version} & \texttt{cargo} package version, e.g. \texttt{0.1.0} & Free text. \\
\texttt{\# prov:host} & Producer hostname & Free text. \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}


\textbf{B.2 Optional keys (stratified outputs):}

When the producing binary is stratum-aware (\texttt{f2\_dual\_mediation},
\texttt{f2\_mediation\_sensitivity}, \texttt{f2\_stratum\_compare}), the preamble is
followed by a single banner line of the form:

\begin{verbatim}
# INPUT STRATUM = canonical          (free baseline)
# INPUT STRATUM = wd0                (Pearl CDE on weight_decay)
# INPUT STRATUM = warmup0            (Pearl CDE on warmup_steps_unquantized)
# INPUT STRATUM = mixed              (concatenated; causally undefined)
\end{verbatim}

A \texttt{mixed} banner causes downstream binaries to refuse to emit a
verdict; see \cref{sec:3.5.3}.

\textbf{B.3 Validation exit codes (\texttt{f2\_provenance\_check}):}

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Exit 0 --- PASS.} All required keys present, schema string matches current \texttt{TRAINER\_INTERNALS\_SCHEMA}, git SHA matches \texttt{HEAD}. Safe to consume downstream.
\item \textbf{Exit 1 --- WARN.} Keys present, schema matches, but git SHA differs from \texttt{HEAD}. Older commit may still be valid; reviewer should confirm intentional.
\item \textbf{Exit 2 --- FAIL (schema).} Schema mismatch OR required key missing. CSV is not safe for downstream consumption; the BPB numbers cannot be vouched for.
\item \textbf{Exit 3 --- FAIL (no preamble).} No preamble present at all. CSV predates the provenance discipline; quarantine.
\end{itemize}

The exit codes are locked by the
\texttt{f2\_provenance\_check\_exit\_codes} integration suite (six tests covering
the four codes + boundary cases).

\section{Reviewer-grade tooling catalogue}\label{app:e}


The \cref{sec:3.5.1}--\cref{sec:3.5.4} discipline (cf. \cref{sec:3.5.4} closing paragraph) is
operationalized through eight auxiliary scripts under
\texttt{papers/scripts/} that a reviewer can run to verify each invariant
mechanically. Wall-clock figures below assume a \textbf{warm cargo cache}
(prior \texttt{cargo build --release} of \texttt{f2\_to\_jsonl},
\texttt{f2\_mediation\_sensitivity}, \texttt{f2\_provenance\_check} and prior
\texttt{cargo test --no-run} for the lib + 10 F2 bins + 7 integration
suites). \textbf{Cold-clone first run is 15--30 minutes}, dominated by
Rust compilation of a 38-binary, 157-dependency workspace; on
subsequent invocations the cache is warm and the numbers below hold.

\textbf{Required external tools}: \texttt{xelatex}, \texttt{bibtex}, \texttt{pdftotext} (from
poppler); \texttt{python3} with \texttt{matplotlib} + \texttt{numpy}; \texttt{zip}; the Rust
toolchain (\texttt{cargo}). The CI gate aborts on the first missing
dependency; we do not stub any of them.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{\texttt{papers/scripts/cross\_reference\_audit.py}} (< 1 s warm) --- verify every paper-internal §X.Y reference resolves to a header, every arXiv citation is well-formed, every backtick file/binary mention points at a real path under \texttt{src/bin/} or \texttt{tests/}.

the live \texttt{verify\_cross\_paper\_consistency.py} \texttt{\_CLAIMS} lists), the documented-vs-extracted-consistency verifier (binds \cref{sec:1} sub-bullet description metadata like "6 reports (2 full + 4 stub)" to live verifier-source state), and the burn-down-history verifier (asserts the FALLBACK\_BASELINES trajectory most-recent entry matches the live sidecar state), the alias-round-trip verifier (asserts CLASS\_LABEL\_ALIASES is bijective on the gate's actual class names --- every alias resolves to a live class, every class has at least one alias), the module-cache-consistency verifier (asserts the \_gate\_utils import\_gate cache contract holds), the floating-loop-anchor verifier (gates "as of Loop N" anchors against the \cref{sec:7} lead loop with 1-loop in-flight tolerance), the anchor-loop-coverage verifier (asserts every CHANGELOG \cref{sec:10} Loop-N entry has $\geq$1 matching commit on HEAD), the dependency-graph verifier (asserts the inter-gate import topology is acyclic and respects STAGES execution order), the tier-classification verifier (asserts STAGES/STAGE\_TIERS parity + contiguity), the burn-down-trajectory verifier (asserts the breadcrumb is loop-monotonic + non-increasing), the \cref{sec:10}-authority verifier (asserts every CI-gate verify\_*.py stage has a matching CHANGELOG \cref{sec:10} entry), the gate-authoring-guide-drift verifier (asserts the discipline doc and live code agree on the breadcrumb label-class regex), the deadline-freshness verifier (asserts every dated AOE deadline in \texttt{papers/SUBMISSION\_CHECKLIST.md} \cref{sec:4} is today-or-future or annotated as historical), the tex-anonymization verifier (scans the anonymized \texttt{.tex} build artifact for bare Loop-N, branch name, PII identifiers, internal email domain leaks, and SHA-like tokens --- closes the converter-side leak class not caught by the markdown-source-only anonymizer ratchet), and the format-microbench-freshness verifier (asserts the format-zoo grid summary JSON in \texttt{.trinity/results/format\_microbench\_grid/} exists with the expected schema and all 60 per-cell JSONs are present --- gates the \cref{sec:9.4} format-zoo headline table against silent regeneration regressions). Exits 0 only if every stage passes. The catalogue above is the original 8 the paper relied on at draft time; the additional 34 are documented in the follow-up paper's \cref{sec:5.4}. Per-introduction history (which loop added which gate) is enumerated in \texttt{papers/CHANGELOG.md} \cref{sec:10}. (Earlier drafts wrote "seven catalogued + ten additional", which an adversarial pass corrected.)
\end{itemize}

\texttt{papers/tmlr\_submission\_kit/pack\_supplementary.sh} chains
\texttt{papers/scripts/figure\_regen.sh} + \texttt{f2\_provenance\_check} +
\texttt{papers/scripts/verify\_paper\_metadata.py} as a three-stage pre-flight
before building the supplementary zip; any single failure aborts
the pack. The intent is that no supplementary artifact ever ships
without all invariants verified at bundle time.
